content.text:
Overall, Bangkok Prep has a good reputation. It's usually described as a well-established, mid-sized British school with a friendly community, rather than one of Bangkok's elite "big brand" schools. Whether it's worth it depends on what you need. Here's what I found.

## Strengths

**Independent reviews are positive.** The Good Schools Guide says it is
"giving the bigger brand schools a run for their money"
and calls it one of the most popular diverse and supportive British schools in Thailand. It also praises the
unique forest campus and fabulous community spirit.
Another review site calls it
a well-established, CIS-accredited British international school in central Bangkok with a clean age 2–18 pathway across two campuses

.

**Exam results have improved.**

In 2025, 58 per cent of IGCSE results were graded 9-7 and at A level 52 per cent grades A*/A (72 per cent A*-B). In 2024, 46 per cent at 9-7 at IGCSE, 35 per cent at A*/A at A level (64 per cent A*-B).

These figures are reported by the school, and they vary from year to year.

**University places.**
In 2025 university destinations included in the US Brown University; Cornell University; New York University (NYU); Rhode Island School of Design; University of Michigan

and UCLA. The school's full list also includes many mid-ranked UK, Thai and Japanese universities, so ask what a typical graduate goes on to do.

**Accreditation.** The school says it is
accredited by the Council of International Schools (CIS) and ONESQA

, and is a member of FOBISIA and ISAT.

**Community.** It has
60+ nationalities
, and parents say
the board of governors and directors are very visible and often spotted at school functions

.

## Things to weigh up

- **Change of owner:**
In 2023, Bangkok Prep joined International Schools Partnership
, a global for-profit school group. Some older parent reviews liked that the school was
"not directed by a large financial company"

. That no longer applies, so ask current parents whether anything has changed since the takeover.
- **No graded inspection:** One reviewer says it's held back from the top tier
only by the absence of a published independent inspection (BSO/ISI) rating.
- **No IB:**
Families wanting the IB Diploma must look elsewhere.

The school offers IGCSE, A Levels and BTEC instead.
- **English support for older children:**
No dedicated, named EAL programme for older entrants is detailed publicly.

This matters if your child is still learning English.
- **Some negative reviews:** One parent wrote that
the early years of the junior school is good, but the senior school is seriously lacking in academic rigour.

That's only one review, and it's outnumbered by positive ones, but it's worth asking about secondary teaching specifically.
- **Fees:** For 2024/25, one site lists
annual fees of THB 548,500–782,000

, plus one-off fees for registration and placement. That's in the "premium" band, though it's cheaper than the top-tier schools. Download the official 2025–26 fee schedule from the school's website.

## Is it worth it?

It's likely a good fit if you want:
- a British curriculum from nursery all the way to age 18
- a warm, diverse school that isn't too large
- a strong focus on sustainability
- good, but not cut-throat, academics
- a lower price than Bangkok's most expensive schools

You may want to look elsewhere if you want:
- the IB
- a very academic, high-pressure secondary school
- a school with a graded UK inspection
- strong English support for an older child

Before you decide:
1. Visit both the primary and secondary campuses.
2. Ask for results for the last 3–5 years and recent university destinations.
3. Ask how long teachers stay and how it has changed under ISP.
4. Talk to current parents with children the same age as yours, for example through the parents' association, Friends of Bangkok Prep.

If you tell me your child's age, how well they speak English, your budget and what you're looking for, I can help compare it with similar schools.
